A 19th-century academic oil painting with a smooth, finely blended surface: soft glazed transitions, delicate fine detail, minimal visible brushstrokes, no heavy impasto, no rough texture. Strong light and shadow from a single warm source (a lamp, a torch, a fire, a low sun) or from heavy overcast, with deep chiaroscuro. Palette of umber, ochre, gold, olive and near-black, with occasional cool accents. The manner of a romantic landscape, a grand historical scene, or a natural-history study of a creature painted as if real. A low, close viewpoint. Wet, reflective stone where there is stone; ancient architecture where there is architecture; one saturated subject held against darkness; scale shown by something small beside something vast. Quiet, watchful, ominous mood. No text, no lettering, no border, no frame, no grid texture, not photographic.

A line of townspeople waiting at dawn to have their scales read by a single standing figure, at a gate on a high clay bank in low, wet reed country, on a cold misty morning in autumn, seen from low in the yard a few paces behind the figure, looking out through the gate along the waiting line. A gate on the top of a high clay bank: two timber posts and a lintel standing alone, with no wall and no fence on either side, the gate open. Beyond it a yard of beaten clay, and a long, low house with clay walls and a reed roof, the largest roof in the town, its one door facing the yard. To one side of the yard a drum as wide as a cart wheel hangs on a frame of heavy timber. At the foot of the nearer gatepost stands a tall, lean figure in a long coat with many deep pockets, the coat the first thing seen. The face is a middle-aged mortal's, plain, with steady eyes that watch as a man watches a scale while the pans settle. The hands are stained with ink and green verdigris. A pair of small, plain brass scales, slightly dented, hangs at the belt. Seen from behind or in deep shadow, the head turned away or lost in darkness, no face visible. Here the figure holds up, by its cord, a small hand balance of wood and cord with two little wooden pans, and is watching the pans settle; the small brass scales stand on the clay at its feet with a few small nested brass cups beside them. The low sun is just up, out of frame to the right, and comes level through the gate: it lights the brass, the stained hand holding the cord and the nearest faces in the line gold, and leaves the figure's back, the yard and the house wall in deep shadow. The line runs away from the gate down the bank and is lost in the mist: wiry, sun-dark boat people with strings of dried fish over their shoulders, broad, stocky people in clay-stained clothes, weathered, quiet people with covered baskets, a few tall, pale people, each holding a small balance or a beam with clay pans, the nearest one, a wiry woman, with her hands held ready to take her balance back. Beside the gatepost two men of the town's watch stand with plain spears grounded, looking at the line and not at the figure. Beyond and below the bank, mist lies on a wide slow channel with flat-bottomed boats drawn up on a landing, and tawny reeds stretch away flat to the sky. No metal armor, no walls, no stone buildings. The small bright brass scales on the clay beside the long dark waiting line and the wide flat country give the scale.
